{"parentUuid":"427fe792-c897-4f39-a87a-a1f20b37efcb","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"0d38cbbf-db22-4bcd-bf4d-0dfd07337e74","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01LZjoeVzaUFk5Q66y8Ec5nA","type":"tool_result","content":"title:\tT05 — Coach manages pages; pages build the navigation\nstate:\tOPEN\nauthor:\tRafaelFrias1\nlabels:\tready-for-agent, ticket\ncomments:\t0\nassignees:\t\nprojects:\t\nmilestone:\t\nissue-type:\t\nparent:\t\nsub-issues:\t\nsub-issues-completed:\t\nblocked-by:\tRafaelFrias1/iphs400-mp2-cms#5\nblocking:\tRafaelFrias1/iphs400-mp2-cms#7\nnumber:\t6\n--\n## Parent\n\n#1\n\n## What to build\n\nThe Coach creates and edits the Season Schedule (with live-scoring links), Travel Lineup and Recruiting pages. Pages are admin-only, and editors are refused every page action. Published pages appear in the public site's navigation on every page. The home page shows the Travel Lineup first, then the newest posts, so a player sees \"am I traveling\" and \"when is practice\" on one screen. The public site is designed for phones first.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] An admin can create, edit, publish, unpublish and delete pages, with the same fields as posts (title, unique slug, Markdown body, status, author, timestamps)\n- [ ] An editor is refused (403) on every page action, including direct requests\n- [ ] The public navigation lists every published page and no draft pages, on every public page\n- [ ] The home page shows the published page with slug `travel-lineup` first (if one exists), then published posts newest first\n- [ ] Page changes run a site update under the same rules as posts\n- [ ] Public pages are readable on a ~375px-wide phone with no horizontal scroll\n- [ ] All output paths remain relative, and Markdown remains sanitized\n- [ ] The demo seed adds the three pages (Season Schedule, Travel Lineup, Recruiting) and a few posts, at least one draft and one published\n\n## Blocked by\n\n- T04 (#5)\n## Problem Statement\n\nThe Kenyon men's golf team runs on the team group chat and the coach's emails. Important details are buried within a day, so players ask the same questions every week: when is practice, where is qualifying, am I traveling. Parents can't easily find where the next tournament is or how to follow live scoring. Recruits email the coach for basic information and results. The official athletics site has results, but someone outside the team updates it, sometimes days late, and it says nothing about practice or travel.\n\nThe coach, captain and team manager are not technical. The coach doesn't want to learn new software mid-season. Some content has to be protected: only the coach may change the travel lineup and qualifying results, only the coach may edit the recruiting page (NCAA rules), and editors must never delete past results.\n\n## Solution\n\nA small CMS for the team. Content is written on **the team laptop** in a local admin console, and a static public site, built for phones first, is updated on GitHub Pages.\n\n- The **Coach** (admin) owns every **page** (Season Schedule, Travel Lineup, Recruiting) and every **qualifying result**, and manages **accounts**.\n- The **Captain** and **Team manager** (editors) write **posts**: the weekly **practice schedule** and **tournament recaps**. They can change only their own posts.\n- Publishing is one click. Any change to published content triggers a **site update**: the public site is rebuilt and deployed automatically (ADR-004). If the deploy fails, the change is not saved, so the console and the website always agree.\n- A **reader** opens the home page on their phone and sees the Travel Lineup, then the newest posts (including this week's practice schedule). The nav links to every page.\n\nVocabulary follows `CONTEXT.md`.\n\n## User Stories\n\n### Login and accounts\n1. As the Coach, I want to log in with my email and password, so that only I can reach the coach-only parts of the console.\n2. As the Captain, I want to log in with my own account, so that my posts carry my name.\n3. As any account holder, I want to log out, so that the next person on the team laptop can't post as me.\n4. As the Coach, I want passwords stored only as argon2 hashes, so that a copied database doesn't reveal anyone's password.\n5. As any account holder, I want a wrong password to give a generic error, so that nobody can tell which emails have accounts.\n6. As a reader or someone who isn't logged in, I want every console URL to send me to the login page, so that the console is never usable without an account.\n7. As the Coach, I want to create an account for this season's Captain with the editor role, so that they can post the practice schedule.\n8. As the Coach, I want to create an account for this season's Team manager with the editor role, so that they can write recaps.\n9. As the Coach, I want to change an account's role, so that I can correct a role given by mistake.\n10. As the Coach, I want to deactivate a graduated Captain's account, so that they can no longer log in.\n11. As a deactivated Captain, I am refused at login even with the right password, so that former team members can't post.\n12. As the Coach, I want a deactivated account's published posts to stay on the site under its name, so that last season's record isn't lost.\n13. As an admin, I am prevented from deactivating my own account, so that the site always keeps an admin.\n14. As the Webmaster, I want a backup admin account, so that I can recover the site if the Coach is locked out.\n15. As an editor, I am refused the account-management screens, including by typing the URL directly, so that only admins manage accounts (field notes: WordPress hid Users *and* denied the direct link).\n\n### Posts\n16. As the Captain, I want to write a practice schedule post with a title and a Markdown body, so that I can format times and places as a list.\n17. As the Captain, I want to save a post as a draft, so that I can finish it later without anyone seeing it.\n18. As the Captain, I want to publish my post with one click, next to Save draft, so that publishing isn't a two-step chore (field notes).\n19. As the Captain, I want the slug generated from the title and made unique automatically (practice-schedule, practice-schedule-2, …), so that I never have to type or think about a slug.\n20. As an admin, I want to edit a slug if needed, so that an important post can have a clean URL.\n21. As the Team manager, I want to write a tournament recap (text only), so that alumni and parents know how the team did.\n22. As the Coach, I want to post qualifying results, so that players and recruits can see them.\n23. As an editor, I want to edit and delete only my own posts, so that the Captain can't change the Coach's results and the Team manager can't change the practice schedule.\n24. As an editor, I am refused when I try to edit or delete someone else's post, even through a direct request, so that the rule holds when the button is hidden.\n25. As the Coach, I want to edit or delete any post, so that I can correct mistakes or remove a botched result.\n26. As any author, I want each post to show its author and its created and updated times, so that readers know how current it is.\n27. As an editor, I want to unpublish my own post, so that I can take down something posted by mistake.\n\n### Pages\n28. As the Coach, I want to create and edit the Season Schedule page, including live-scoring links, so that parents know where the next tournament is and how to follow it.\n29. As the Coach, I want to update the Travel Lineup page in place once, so that I stop texting it to eight people.\n30. As the Coach, I want to edit the Recruiting page with my contact details, so that recruits can reach me without emailing for basics, and so that its content stays NCAA-compliant.\n31. As an editor, I am refused all page creation, editing and deletion, so that every coach-only page is protected by one simple rule.\n32. As a reader, I want every published page in the site navigation, so that I can find the schedule, lineup and recruiting info from any page.\n33. As the Coach, I want draft pages to stay out of the navigation, so that a half-written page never shows up.\n\n### Admin console\n34. As the Coach, I want a dashboard with counts of posts and pages by status, so that I can see what's in draft at a glance.\n35. As any account holder, I want posts and pages in one content list, so that I don't have to hunt for separate menus (field notes).\n36. As any account holder, I want one filter bar on that list (status first, then type and author), so that the status filter isn't hidden away (field notes).\n37. As any account holder, I want to preview the rendered Markdown before publishing, so that I can check formatting.\n38. As an editor, I want the console to show only the actions I'm allowed (no page or account controls), so that I'm not confused by buttons that would fail.\n\n### Publishing and the public site\n39. As the Captain, I want my published post to be on the website without any extra step, so that players see the schedule right away.\n40. As the Coach, I want the site to update automatically whenever I publish, edit, unpublish or delete published content, so that I never have to remember a second button.\n41. As the Coach, editing the Travel Lineup without wifi, I want an error and my typed text kept in the form, with the live lineup left unchanged, so that I can retry with wifi without retyping anything.\n42. As an editor, if a site update fails when I publish, I want my post to stay a draft and be told to try again later, so that \"Published\" in the console always means \"on the website\".\n43. As a player, I want the home page to show the Travel Lineup first and then the newest posts, so that one page on my phone answers \"am I traveling\" and \"when is practice\".\n44. As a parent, I want the Season Schedule in the navigation, so that I can find the next tournament and its live-scoring link.\n45. As a recruit, I want to find results and the coach's contact without emailing, so that I can evaluate the program on my own.\n46. As an alumnus, I want recaps and results listed newest first, so that I can follow how the team is doing.\n47. As a reader, I want the public site readable on a phone with no horizontal scrolling, so that I can check it at the course.\n48. As a reader, I never see draft content, so that unfinished posts stay private.\n49. As a reader, I'm protected from script injection in any post or page, so that a pasted snippet can't run code in my browser.\n50. As the Webmaster, I want every link and asset in the public site to use a relative path, so that the site works from the GitHub Pages subfolder.\n\n## Implementation Decisions\n\n- **Roles.** Exactly two: admin and editor. The Coach and the Webmaster are admins; the Captain and Team manager are editors. Accounts are per person and are never deleted, only deactivated.\n- **Permission rules**, enforced on the server for every request, not only by hiding buttons:\n  - Admin: everything.\n  - Editor: create posts; edit, publish, unpublish and delete only posts they authored; no pages; no account management.\n  - Nobody may deactivate their own account.\n  - Qualifying results have no special type. They are protected because the Coach authors them and editors can't touch others' posts.\n- **Content model.** One content item shape, with a kind of `post` or `page`, a title, a unique slug (generated from the title and de-duplicated; admins may edit it), a Markdown body, a status (`draft` | `published`), an author account, and created and updated timestamps. Posts and pages share one table/model and one editor; \"kind\" drives navigation and permissions.\n- **Account model.** Email (unique), argon2 password hash, role, active flag. Login fails for inactive accounts.\n- **Sessions.** Signed session cookies. Every state-changing form carries a CSRF token, and requests without a valid token are rejected.\n- **Markdown.** Rendered with the Markdown library, then sanitized with the HTML sanitizer before it goes anywhere: preview, console, or `site/`. Images are not part of the allowed output.\n- **Site update module.** One operation, \"update the site\": render all published content into `site/`, then deploy it to `gh-pages`. The console runs it after any change to published content: publish, edit of a published item, unpublish, and delete of a published item. Account changes (including deactivation) never trigger one.\n  - The change and the site update form one unit. The change is staged, the site is rebuilt from the would-be state, and the deploy is attempted. Only after a successful deploy is the change committed; on failure it is rolled back and the form is re-shown with the user's input and an error.\n  - Draft-only changes (saving or deleting a draft) never trigger a site update.\n  - The deployer is injected through `create_app()` (default: push `site/` to `gh-pages` via ghp-import; the GitHub token comes from the environment). See ADR-004.\n- **Public site rendering.** Builds on the existing `render_site(out)`. It writes a home page (the Travel Lineup page content if published, then published posts newest first), one HTML file per published post and page, and a navigation built from published pages. Every `href`/`src` is relative. Styling is mobile-first.\n- **Travel Lineup on the home page.** Identified by its slug (`travel-lineup`), not by a new field.\n- **Console.** Login/logout; a dashboard with counts by kind and status; one content list with a single filter bar (status, kind, author); an editor with Save draft and Publish side by side and a Markdown preview; account management (admin only): create, change role, deactivate/reactivate.\n- **CLI.** `cms publish` and `cms deploy` remain for the Webmaster. They call the same site update module.\n- **ADRs respected.** ADR-001 (local console, static public site), ADR-002 (stack, no new dependencies), ADR-004 (publish auto-deploys, failure blocks the change).\n\n## Testing Decisions\n\n- **Good tests check external behaviour only:** HTTP status codes, redirects, what a page shows, and the files written to `site/`. They never inspect internal functions or database rows when a response or an output file can show the same thing.\n- **Seam 1: HTTP.** The existing `TestClient` + `client_as(role)` fixtures in `tests/conftest.py` (prior art: `tests/test_t00.py`). Covers login and logout, deactivated login refusal, CSRF rejection, the editor vs admin permission matrix (including direct requests to forbidden URLs, per the field notes), post/page CRUD, slug de-duplication, dashboard counts, filters, and preview sanitizing.\n- **Seam 2: rendering.** `render_site(out)` into a temporary directory. Covers: drafts never written; Markdown sanitized (`<script>` stripped); nav built from published pages only; the home page shows the Travel Lineup then newest posts; and no root-absolute `href=\"/` or `src=\"/` anywhere.\n- **Seam 3: deployer (new).** `create_app()` accepts a deployer; tests pass a fake that records calls or raises. Covers: publishing calls the deployer once; a draft save never calls it; when the deployer fails, the item keeps its previous state (still draft, or the old published text) and the response re-shows the user's input with an error. No test ever touches the network or GitHub.\n- The demo users seeded for tests are one admin and one editor; permission tests that need a second editor (to prove \"own posts only\") create one through the admin's account-management route.\n\n## Out of Scope\n\n- Photos, media upload and images in posts (recaps are text only).\n- Posting from a phone; the console runs only on the team laptop and is never on the public internet.\n- Search, comments, contact forms, or any server-side feature on the public site.\n- Scheduled (future-dated) publishing and revision history/undo.\n- A separate \"qualifying result\" post type, categories or tags.\n- Password reset by email; self-service sign-up.\n- Multi-site, drag-and-drop page builders, WYSIWYG editors.\n\n## Further Notes\n\n- **Trust risk accepted:** the Captain is a player and could post scores in a practice-schedule post; the CMS relies on trust there rather than a result type.\n- **Operational risk accepted (ADR-004):** the team laptop holds a GitHub push token (from the environment, never committed) and must be online to publish.\n- The client brief's delete rule was revised during grilling: \"Only the coach can delete past results. Editors can never delete them.\"\n- Field-note findings that became requirements: one-click Publish, one filter bar with status first, posts and pages in one list, and access control that denies direct URLs as well as hiding menu items.\n\n# Kenyon Men's Golf CMS\n\nThe team's own site: one place where players, parents, recruits and alumni find the schedule, the travel lineup, results and coach contact, instead of searching the group chat.\n\n## People\n\n**Account**:\nOne person's login, with one role. The Coach creates accounts for each season's Captain and Team manager and deactivates them when the person leaves.\n_Avoid_: user (for the login), member\n\n**Coach**:\nThe head coach. Holds the **admin** role, owns all pages and qualifying results, and manages accounts.\n_Avoid_: owner, superuser\n\n**Captain**:\nThe player who is team captain this season, with their own account. Holds the **editor** role and posts the weekly practice schedule.\n\n**Team manager**:\nThe team manager this season, with their own account. Holds the **editor** role and writes tournament recaps after events.\n_Avoid_: manager (alone), which could be confused with the admin role\n\n**Webmaster**:\nThe person who built and maintains the CMS. Holds a backup **admin** account in case the Coach is locked out.\n_Avoid_: developer, IT\n\n**Admin**:\nThe role with full permissions: all pages, all posts, and managing accounts. An admin can't deactivate their own account or change their own role, so the site always keeps an admin.\n\n**Deactivated**:\nThe state of an account whose person has left (e.g. a graduated Captain). It can no longer log in; it is never deleted.\n_Avoid_: deleted, removed, banned\n\n**Editor**:\nThe role for people who write posts and may change only their own. Editors never touch pages, other people's posts, or accounts.\n_Avoid_: author, contributor\n\n**Reader**:\nAnyone viewing the public site: players, parents, recruits, alumni. Readers have no account.\n_Avoid_: visitor, user\n\n## Content\n\n**Item**:\nA post or a page. All posting happens here; nobody posts from a phone.\n_Avoid_: server, backend","is_error":false}]},"uuid":"6dfc5aa8-6ba5-4d29-8478-686a160b1bc7","timestamp":"2026-10-15T16:36:47.605Z","toolUseResult":{"stdout":"title:\tT05 — Coach manages pages; pages build the navigation\nstate:\tOPEN\nauthor:\tRafaelFrias1\nlabels:\tready-for-agent, ticket\ncomments:\t0\nassignees:\t\nprojects:\t\nmilestone:\t\nissue-type:\t\nparent:\t\nsub-issues:\t\nsub-issues-completed:\t\nblocked-by:\tRafaelFrias1/iphs400-mp2-cms#5\nblocking:\tRafaelFrias1/iphs400-mp2-cms#7\nnumber:\t6\n--\n## Parent\n\n#1\n\n## What to build\n\nThe Coach creates and edits the Season Schedule (with live-scoring links), Travel Lineup and Recruiting pages. Pages are admin-only, and editors are refused every page action. Published pages appear in the public site's navigation on every page. The home page shows the Travel Lineup first, then the newest posts, so a player sees \"am I traveling\" and \"when is practice\" on one screen. The public site is designed for phones first.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] An admin can create, edit, publish, unpublish and delete pages, with the same fields as posts (title, unique slug, Markdown body, status, author, timestamps)\n- [ ] An editor is refused (403) on every page action, including direct requests\n- [ ] The public navigation lists every published page and no draft pages, on every public page\n- [ ] The home page shows the published page with slug `travel-lineup` first (if one exists), then published posts newest first\n- [ ] Page changes run a site update under the same rules as posts\n- [ ] Public pages are readable on a ~375px-wide phone with no horizontal scroll\n- [ ] All output paths remain relative, and Markdown remains sanitized\n- [ ] The demo seed adds the three pages (Season Schedule, Travel Lineup, Recruiting) and a few posts, at least one draft and one published\n\n## Blocked by\n\n- T04 (#5)\n## Problem Statement\n\nThe Kenyon men's golf team runs on the team group chat and the coach's emails. Important details are buried within a day, so players ask the same questions every week: when is practice, where is qualifying, am I traveling. Parents can't easily find where the next tournament is or how to follow live scoring. Recruits email the coach for basic information and results. The official athletics site has results, but someone outside the team updates it, sometimes days late, and it says nothing about practice or travel.\n\nThe coach, captain and team manager are not technical. The coach doesn't want to learn new software mid-season. Some content has to be protected: only the coach may change the travel lineup and qualifying results, only the coach may edit the recruiting page (NCAA rules), and editors must never delete past results.\n\n## Solution\n\nA small CMS for the team. Content is written on **the team laptop** in a local admin console, and a static public site, built for phones first, is updated on GitHub Pages.\n\n- The **Coach** (admin) owns every **page** (Season Schedule, Travel Lineup, Recruiting) and every **qualifying result**, and manages **accounts**.\n- The **Captain** and **Team manager** (editors) write **posts**: the weekly **practice schedule** and **tournament recaps**. They can change only their own posts.\n- Publishing is one click. Any change to published content triggers a **site update**: the public site is rebuilt and deployed automatically (ADR-004). If the deploy fails, the change is not saved, so the console and the website always agree.\n- A **reader** opens the home page on their phone and sees the Travel Lineup, then the newest posts (including this week's practice schedule). The nav links to every page.\n\nVocabulary follows `CONTEXT.md`.\n\n## User Stories\n\n### Login and accounts\n1. As the Coach, I want to log in with my email and password, so that only I can reach the coach-only parts of the console.\n2. As the Captain, I want to log in with my own account, so that my posts carry my name.\n3. As any account holder, I want to log out, so that the next person on the team laptop can't post as me.\n4. As the Coach, I want passwords stored only as argon2 hashes, so that a copied database doesn't reveal anyone's password.\n5. As any account holder, I want a wrong password to give a generic error, so that nobody can tell which emails have accounts.\n6. As a reader or someone who isn't logged in, I want every console URL to send me to the login page, so that the console is never usable without an account.\n7. As the Coach, I want to create an account for this season's Captain with the editor role, so that they can post the practice schedule.\n8. As the Coach, I want to create an account for this season's Team manager with the editor role, so that they can write recaps.\n9. As the Coach, I want to change an account's role, so that I can correct a role given by mistake.\n10. As the Coach, I want to deactivate a graduated Captain's account, so that they can no longer log in.\n11. As a deactivated Captain, I am refused at login even with the right password, so that former team members can't post.\n12. As the Coach, I want a deactivated account's published posts to stay on the site under its name, so that last season's record isn't lost.\n13. As an admin, I am prevented from deactivating my own account, so that the site always keeps an admin.\n14. As the Webmaster, I want a backup admin account, so that I can recover the site if the Coach is locked out.\n15. As an editor, I am refused the account-management screens, including by typing the URL directly, so that only admins manage accounts (field notes: WordPress hid Users *and* denied the direct link).\n\n### Posts\n16. As the Captain, I want to write a practice schedule post with a title and a Markdown body, so that I can format times and places as a list.\n17. As the Captain, I want to save a post as a draft, so that I can finish it later without anyone seeing it.\n18. As the Captain, I want to publish my post with one click, next to Save draft, so that publishing isn't a two-step chore (field notes).\n19. As the Captain, I want the slug generated from the title and made unique automatically (practice-schedule, practice-schedule-2, …), so that I never have to type or think about a slug.\n20. As an admin, I want to edit a slug if needed, so that an important post can have a clean URL.\n21. As the Team manager, I want to write a tournament recap (text only), so that alumni and parents know how the team did.\n22. As the Coach, I want to post qualifying results, so that players and recruits can see them.\n23. As an editor, I want to edit and delete only my own posts, so that the Captain can't change the Coach's results and the Team manager can't change the practice schedule.\n24. As an editor, I am refused when I try to edit or delete someone else's post, even through a direct request, so that the rule holds when the button is hidden.\n25. As the Coach, I want to edit or delete any post, so that I can correct mistakes or remove a botched result.\n26. As any author, I want each post to show its author and its created and updated times, so that readers know how current it is.\n27. As an editor, I want to unpublish my own post, so that I can take down something posted by mistake.\n\n### Pages\n28. As the Coach, I want to create and edit the Season Schedule page, including live-scoring links, so that parents know where the next tournament is and how to follow it.\n29. As the Coach, I want to update the Travel Lineup page in place once, so that I stop texting it to eight people.\n30. As the Coach, I want to edit the Recruiting page with my contact details, so that recruits can reach me without emailing for basics, and so that its content stays NCAA-compliant.\n31. As an editor, I am refused all page creation, editing and deletion, so that every coach-only page is protected by one simple rule.\n32. As a reader, I want every published page in the site navigation, so that I can find the schedule, lineup and recruiting info from any page.\n33. As the Coach, I want draft pages to stay out of the navigation, so that a half-written page never shows up.\n\n### Admin console\n34. As the Coach, I want a dashboard with counts of posts and pages by status, so that I can see what's in draft at a glance.\n35. As any account holder, I want posts and pages in one content list, so that I don't have to hunt for separate menus (field notes).\n36. As any account holder, I want one filter bar on that list (status first, then type and author), so that the status filter isn't hidden away (field notes).\n37. As any account holder, I want to preview the rendered Markdown before publishing, so that I can check formatting.\n38. As an editor, I want the console to show only the actions I'm allowed (no page or account controls), so that I'm not confused by buttons that would fail.\n\n### Publishing and the public site\n39. As the Captain, I want my published post to be on the website without any extra step, so that players see the schedule right away.\n40. As the Coach, I want the site to update automatically whenever I publish, edit, unpublish or delete published content, so that I never have to remember a second button.\n41. As the Coach, editing the Travel Lineup without wifi, I want an error and my typed text kept in the form, with the live lineup left unchanged, so that I can retry with wifi without retyping anything.\n42. As an editor, if a site update fails when I publish, I want my post to stay a draft and be told to try again later, so that \"Published\" in the console always means \"on the website\".\n43. As a player, I want the home page to show the Travel Lineup first and then the newest posts, so that one page on my phone answers \"am I traveling\" and \"when is practice\".\n44. As a parent, I want the Season Schedule in the navigation, so that I can find the next tournament and its live-scoring link.\n45. As a recruit, I want to find results and the coach's contact without emailing, so that I can evaluate the program on my own.\n46. As an alumnus, I want recaps and results listed newest first, so that I can follow how the team is doing.\n47. As a reader, I want the public site readable on a phone with no horizontal scrolling, so that I can check it at the course.\n48. As a reader, I never see draft content, so that unfinished posts stay private.\n49. As a reader, I'm protected from script injection in any post or page, so that a pasted snippet can't run code in my browser.\n50. As the Webmaster, I want every link and asset in the public site to use a relative path, so that the site works from the GitHub Pages subfolder.\n\n## Implementation Decisions\n\n- **Roles.** Exactly two: admin and editor. The Coach and the Webmaster are admins; the Captain and Team manager are editors. Accounts are per person and are never deleted, only deactivated.\n- **Permission rules**, enforced on the server for every request, not only by hiding buttons:\n  - Admin: everything.\n  - Editor: create posts; edit, publish, unpublish and delete only posts they authored; no pages; no account management.\n  - Nobody may deactivate their own account.\n  - Qualifying results have no special type. They are protected because the Coach authors them and editors can't touch others' posts.\n- **Content model.** One content item shape, with a kind of `post` or `page`, a title, a unique slug (generated from the title and de-duplicated; admins may edit it), a Markdown body, a status (`draft` | `published`), an author account, and created and updated timestamps. Posts and pages share one table/model and one editor; \"kind\" drives navigation and permissions.\n- **Account model.** Email (unique), argon2 password hash, role, active flag. Login fails for inactive accounts.\n- **Sessions.** Signed session cookies. Every state-changing form carries a CSRF token, and requests without a valid token are rejected.\n- **Markdown.** Rendered with the Markdown library, then sanitized with the HTML sanitizer before it goes anywhere: preview, console, or `site/`. Images are not part of the allowed output.\n- **Site update module.** One operation, \"update the site\": render all published content into `site/`, then deploy it to `gh-pages`. The console runs it after any change to published content: publish, edit of a published item, unpublish, and delete of a published item. Account changes (including deactivation) never trigger one.\n  - The change and the site update form one unit. The change is staged, the site is rebuilt from the would-be state, and the deploy is attempted. Only after a successful deploy is the change committed; on failure it is rolled back and the form is re-shown with the user's input and an error.\n  - Draft-only changes (saving or deleting a draft) never trigger a site update.\n  - The deployer is injected through `create_app()` (default: push `site/` to `gh-pages` via ghp-import; the GitHub token comes from the environment). See ADR-004.\n- **Public site rendering.** Builds on the existing `render_site(out)`. It writes a home page (the Travel Lineup page content if published, then published posts newest first), one HTML file per published post and page, and a navigation built from published pages. Every `href`/`src` is relative. Styling is mobile-first.\n- **Travel Lineup on the home page.** Identified by its slug (`travel-lineup`), not by a new field.\n- **Console.** Login/logout; a dashboard with counts by kind and status; one content list with a single filter bar (status, kind, author); an editor with Save draft and Publish side by side and a Markdown preview; account management (admin only): create, change role, deactivate/reactivate.\n- **CLI.** `cms publish` and `cms deploy` remain for the Webmaster. They call the same site update module.\n- **ADRs respected.** ADR-001 (local console, static public site), ADR-002 (stack, no new dependencies), ADR-004 (publish auto-deploys, failure blocks the change).\n\n## Testing Decisions\n\n- **Good tests check external behaviour only:** HTTP status codes, redirects, what a page shows, and the files written to `site/`. They never inspect internal functions or database rows when a response or an output file can show the same thing.\n- **Seam 1: HTTP.** The existing `TestClient` + `client_as(role)` fixtures in `tests/conftest.py` (prior art: `tests/test_t00.py`). Covers login and logout, deactivated login refusal, CSRF rejection, the editor vs admin permission matrix (including direct requests to forbidden URLs, per the field notes), post/page CRUD, slug de-duplication, dashboard counts, filters, and preview sanitizing.\n- **Seam 2: rendering.** `render_site(out)` into a temporary directory. Covers: drafts never written; Markdown sanitized (`<script>` stripped); nav built from published pages only; the home page shows the Travel Lineup then newest posts; and no root-absolute `href=\"/` or `src=\"/` anywhere.\n- **Seam 3: deployer (new).** `create_app()` accepts a deployer; tests pass a fake that records calls or raises. Covers: publishing calls the deployer once; a draft save never calls it; when the deployer fails, the item keeps its previous state (still draft, or the old published text) and the response re-shows the user's input with an error. No test ever touches the network or GitHub.\n- The demo users seeded for tests are one admin and one editor; permission tests that need a second editor (to prove \"own posts only\") create one through the admin's account-management route.\n\n## Out of Scope\n\n- Photos, media upload and images in posts (recaps are text only).\n- Posting from a phone; the console runs only on the team laptop and is never on the public internet.\n- Search, comments, contact forms, or any server-side feature on the public site.\n- Scheduled (future-dated) publishing and revision history/undo.\n- A separate \"qualifying result\" post type, categories or tags.\n- Password reset by email; self-service sign-up.\n- Multi-site, drag-and-drop page builders, WYSIWYG editors.\n\n## Further Notes\n\n- **Trust risk accepted:** the Captain is a player and could post scores in a practice-schedule post; the CMS relies on trust there rather than a result type.\n- **Operational risk accepted (ADR-004):** the team laptop holds a GitHub push token (from the environment, never committed) and must be online to publish.\n- The client brief's delete rule was revised during grilling: \"Only the coach can delete past results. Editors can never delete them.\"\n- Field-note findings that became requirements: one-click Publish, one filter bar with status first, posts and pages in one list, and access control that denies direct URLs as well as hiding menu items.\n\n# Kenyon Men's Golf CMS\n\nThe team's own site: one place where players, parents, recruits and alumni find the schedule, the travel lineup, results and coach contact, instead of searching the group chat.\n\n## People\n\n**Account**:\nOne person's login, with one role. Every href and src is RELATIVE (\"style.css\", \"posts/x.html\"), never\n     root-absolute (\"/style.css\"), because Pages serves this from a subfolder.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport shutil\nfrom datetime import datetime\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom jinja2 import Environment, FileSystemLoader, select_autoescape\n\nfrom app import content, settings\nfrom app.content import Item, Kind, Status\nfrom app.markdown import render_markdown\n\nCSS = \"\"\"/* Minimal starter styles — make them yours. */\n:root { color-scheme: light dark; }\nbody { font: 16px/1.6 system-ui, sans-serif; margin: 0 auto; max-width: 42rem; padding: 1rem; }\nheader a { font-weight: 700; text-decoration: none; }\nheader .console { float: right; font-weight: 400; }\nmain { margin-block: 2rem; }\n.byline { color: GrayText; font-size: 0.9rem; }\n\"\"\"\n\n\ndef byline(email: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"The author's name on the public site: the part of the email before @.\n\n    The full email is never published, so readers can't harvest it (ADR-005).\n    \"\"\"\n    return email.split(\"@\", 1)[0]\n\n\ndef reader_date(timestamp: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"An ISO UTC timestamp as readers see it, 'Oct 14, 2026', in the team\n    laptop's time zone, so an evening post isn't dated tomorrow.\"\"\"\n    return datetime.fromisoformat(timestamp).astimezone().strftime(\"%b %d, %Y\")\n\n\ndef environment() -> Environment:\n    env = Environment(\n        loader=FileSystemLoader(str(settings.TEMPLATES)),\n        autoescape=select_autoescape([\"html\"]),\n    )\n    env.filters[\"byline\"] = byline\n    env.filters[\"reader_date\"] = reader_date\n    return env\n\n\ndef published_posts(db_path: Path) -> list[Item]:\n    \"\"\"Newest first. A database that doesn't exist yet (a fresh clone) has none.\"\"\"\n    if not db_path.exists():\n        return []\n    return content.list_items(db_path, Kind.POST, Status.PUBLISHED)\n\n\ndef home_html(posts: list[Item], preview: bool = False) -> str:\n    \"\"\"index.html: the published posts, newest first.\n\n    A preview (the console's /) also links to the console; site/ never does.\n    \"\"\"\n    return environment().get_template(\"public/home.html\").render(\n        title=settings.SITE_TITLE, posts=posts, css_path=\"style.css\",\n        home_path=\"index.html\", console_path=\"admin\" if preview else None,\n    )\n\n\ndef post_html(post: Item, preview: bool = False) -> str:\n    \"\"\"posts/<slug>.html: one published post, its Markdown sanitized.\"\"\"\n    return environment().get_template(\"public/post.html\").render(\n        title=settings.SITE_TITLE, post=post, body=render_markdown(post.body),\n        css_path=\"../style.css\", home_path=\"../index.html\",\n        console_path=\"../admin\" if preview else None,\n    )\n\n\ndef render_site(out: Path | None = None, db_path: Path | None = None) -> Path:\n    \"\"\"Rebuild `out` from scratch with every published post in `db_path`.\"\"\"\n    out = out or settings.SITE\n    posts = published_posts(db_path or settings.DATABASE_PATH)\n    if out.exists():\n        shutil.rmtree(out)\n    (out / \"posts\").mkdir(parents=True)\n    (out / \"style.css\").write_text(CSS)\n    (out / \"index.html\").write_text(home_html(posts))\n    for post in posts:\n        (out / \"posts\" / f\"{post.slug}.html\").write_text(post_html(post))\n    return out\n\n\ndef update_site(db_path: Path, out: Path) -> Path:\n    \"\"\"Run a site update after a change to published content.\"\"\"\n    return render_site(out, db_path)\n\"\"\"Posts: any logged-in account writes them; editors change only their own.\n\nThe form's buttons are sent as `action`. Preview re-shows the form with the\nsanitized, rendered Markdown and saves nothing. Save keeps the post's status:\na draft stays a draft, a published post stays published. Publish saves and\npublishes in one click. Unpublish and Delete are separate small forms.\n\nAny change to published content (publish, saving a published post, unpublish,\ndeleting a published post) runs a site update; draft-only changes never do.\nEditors get 403 on someone else's post, whether they follow a link or type\nthe URL. Only admins may set a slug by hand; an editor's slug field, if sent\nanyway, is ignored.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, Form, HTTPException, {"parentUuid":"8a97e464-5557-41d7-b754-af28af25f592","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"0d38cbbf-db22-4bcd-bf4d-0dfd07337e74","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01HhBp9X95NUsBcFrKRREhXm","type":"tool_result","content":"\"\"\"Content items: posts and pages share one shape (see CONTEXT.md).\n\nAn item has a kind (post or page), a title, a unique slug, a Markdown body, a\nstatus (draft or published), an author account and created/updated\ntimestamps. The slug is generated from the title and de-duplicated\n(\"practice-schedule\", \"practice-schedule-2\", ...); only admins set one by hand.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport re\nimport sqlite3\nimport unicodedata\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\nfrom datetime import UTC, datetime\nfrom enum import StrEnum\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom app import db\nfrom app.accounts import Account\n\n\nclass Kind(StrEnum):\n    POST = \"post\"\n    PAGE = \"page\"\n\n\nclass Status(StrEnum):\n    DRAFT = \"draft\"\n    PUBLISHED = \"published\"\n\n\nclass SlugTaken(Exception):\n    \"\"\"Raised when an admin sets a slug another item already uses.\"\"\"\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass Item:\n    id: int\n    kind: Kind\n    title: str\n    slug: str\n    body: str\n    status: Status\n    author_id: int\n    author_email: str\n    created_at: str\n    updated_at: str\n\n\ndef can_change(account: Account, item: Item) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Admins change anything; editors change only posts they wrote.\"\"\"\n    return account.is_admin or (item.kind is Kind.POST\n                                and item.author_id == account.id)\n\n\ndef slugify(text: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"'Practice Schedule!' -> 'practice-schedule'; '' when nothing is left.\"\"\"\n    ascii_text = (unicodedata.normalize(\"NFKD\", text)\n                  .encode(\"ascii\", \"ignore\").decode())\n    return re.sub(r\"[^a-z0-9]+\", \"-\", ascii_text.lower()).strip(\"-\")\n\n\ndef _now() -> str:\n    return datetime.now(UTC).isoformat(timespec=\"microseconds\")\n\n\n_SELECT = \"\"\"\nSELECT items.*, accounts.email AS author_email\nFROM items JOIN accounts ON accounts.id = items.author_id\n\"\"\"\n\n\ndef _from_row(row) -> Item:\n    return Item(id=row[\"id\"], kind=Kind(row[\"kind\"]), title=row[\"title\"],\n                slug=row[\"slug\"], body=row[\"body\"], status=Status(row[\"status\"]),\n                author_id=row[\"author_id\"], author_email=row[\"author_email\"],\n                created_at=row[\"created_at\"], updated_at=row[\"updated_at\"])\n\n\ndef _unique_slug(conn: sqlite3.Connection, title: str, kind: Kind) -> str:\n    base = slugify(title) or kind.value\n    taken = {row[\"slug\"] for row in conn.execute(\n        \"SELECT slug FROM items WHERE slug = ? OR slug LIKE ?\",\n        (base, f\"{base}-%\"))}\n    slug, n = base, 2\n    while slug in taken:\n        slug, n = f\"{base}-{n}\", n + 1\n    return slug\n\n\ndef create_item(db_path: Path, kind: Kind, title: str, body: str,\n                author: Account, status: Status = Status.DRAFT) -> Item:\n    now = _now()\n    with db.connect(db_path) as conn:\n        cursor = conn.execute(\n            \"INSERT INTO items (kind, title, slug, body, status, author_id,\"\n            \" created_at, updated_at) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)\",\n            (kind, title, _unique_slug(conn, title, kind), body, status,\n             author.id, now, now),\n        )\n    return get_item(db_path, cursor.lastrowid)\n\n\ndef get_item(db_path: Path, item_id: int) -> Item | None:\n    with db.connect(db_path) as conn:\n        row = conn.execute(_SELECT + \"WHERE items.id = ?\", (item_id,)).fetchone()\n    return _from_row(row) if row else None\n\n\ndef list_items(db_path: Path, kind: Kind,\n               status: Status | None = None) -> list[Item]:\n    \"\"\"Newest first; only items with `status` when one is given.\"\"\"\n    with db.connect(db_path) as conn:\n        rows = conn.execute(\n            _SELECT + \"WHERE kind = ? AND status = COALESCE(?, status)\"\n            \" ORDER BY created_at DESC, items.id DESC\", (kind, status)).fetchall()\n    return [_from_row(row) for row in rows]\n\n\ndef update_item(db_path: Path, item_id: int, title: str, body: str,\n                slug: str | None = None, status: Status | None = None) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Change title and body; change the slug and status too when given.\n\n    Raises SlugTaken if the new slug belongs to another item.\n    \"\"\"\n    try:\n        with db.connect(db_path) as conn:\n            conn.execute(\n                \"UPDATE items SET title = ?, body = ?, slug = COALESCE(?, slug),\"\n                \" status = COALESCE(?, status), updated_at = ? WHERE id = ?\",\n                (title, body, slug, status, _now(), item_id),\n            )\n    except sqlite3.IntegrityError as exc:\n        raise SlugTaken(slug) from exc\n\n\ndef set_status(db_path: Path, item_id: int, status: Status) -> None:\n    with db.connect(db_path) as conn:\n        conn.execute(\"UPDATE items SET status = ?, updated_at = ? WHERE id = ?\",\n                     (status, _now(), item_id))\n\n\ndef delete_item(db_path: Path, item_id: int) -> None:\n    with db.connect(db_path) as conn:\n        conn.execute(\"DELETE FROM items WHERE id = ?\", (item_id,))\n\"\"\"The FastAPI application.\n\nThe admin console lives under /admin and needs a login (/login); a preview\nof the public site answers at /. Routes live in their own modules under\napp/routes/ and are included here. Keep this file small.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom fastapi import FastAPI, Request\nfrom fastapi.responses import RedirectResponse\nfrom starlette.middleware.sessions import SessionMiddleware\n\nfrom app import db, settings\nfrom app.routes import accounts, auth, console, posts, public\nfrom app.web import LoginRequired\n\n\ndef create_app(db_path: Path | None = None,\n               site_dir: Path | None = None) -> FastAPI:\n    app = FastAPI(title=\"IPHS 400 MP2 CMS\")\n    app.state.db_path = db_path or settings.DATABASE_PATH\n    # Where site updates write; tests pass a temporary directory.\n    app.state.site_dir = site_dir or settings.SITE\n    db.init(app.state.db_path)\n\n    # Signed session cookie that ends when the browser closes (shared laptop).\n    app.add_middleware(SessionMiddleware, secret_key=settings.SECRET_KEY,\n                       session_cookie=\"cms_session\", max_age=None,\n                       same_site=\"lax\")\n\n    @app.exception_handler(LoginRequired)\n    def to_login(request: Request, exc: LoginRequired):\n        return RedirectResponse(\"/login\", status_code=303)\n\n    app.include_router(auth.router)\n    app.include_router(console.router)\n    app.include_router(accounts.router)\n    app.include_router(posts.router)\n    app.include_router(public.router)\n    return app\n\n\napp = create_app()\n\"\"\"Demo data: one admin and one editor, so the console is usable straight away.\n\nscripts/seed_demo.py calls this with passwords from the environment; the tests\ncall it with fixed ones. Running it again leaves existing accounts alone.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom app import accounts, db\nfrom app.accounts import Role\n\nDEMO_EMAILS = {\n    Role.ADMIN: \"admin@example.test\",\n    Role.EDITOR: \"editor@example.test\",\n}\n\n\ndef seed_demo(db_path: Path, admin_password: str, editor_password: str) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"Create the demo accounts that do not exist yet; return the emails created.\"\"\"\n    db.init(db_path)\n    created = []\n    for role, password in ((Role.ADMIN, admin_password), (Role.EDITOR, editor_password)):\n        email = DEMO_EMAILS[role]\n        if accounts.find_by_email(db_path, email) is None:\n            accounts.create_account(db_path, email, password, role)\n            created.append(email)\n    return created\n#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"Create demo data so a grader (and you) can use the CMS immediately.\n\n    set -a; . ./.env; set +a\n    uv run python scripts/seed_demo.py\n\nCreates one admin and one editor account (app/seed.py), with passwords read\nfrom CMS_ADMIN_PASSWORD and CMS_EDITOR_PASSWORD, never hard-coded. Later\ntickets add demo posts and pages here.\n\nThe rubric expects this to run clean on a fresh clone with .env.example values\n(item E4), because the database itself is never committed.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport os\nimport sys\n\nfrom app import settings\nfrom app.seed import DEMO_EMAILS, seed_demo\n\n\ndef main() -> int:\n    admin_pw = os.environ.get(\"CMS_ADMIN_PASSWORD\")\n    editor_pw = os.environ.get(\"CMS_EDITOR_PASSWORD\")\n    if not admin_pw or not editor_pw:\n        print(\"Set CMS_ADMIN_PASSWORD and CMS_EDITOR_PASSWORD in .env \"\n              \"(copy .env.example).\")\n        return 1\n\n    created = seed_demo(settings.DATABASE_PATH, admin_pw, editor_pw)\n    for role, email in DEMO_EMAILS.items():\n        state = \"created\" if email in created else \"already exists\"\n        print(f\"{role:6}  {email}  ({state})\")\n    print(f\"Database: {settings.DATABASE_PATH}\")\n    return 0\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    sys.exit(main())\n\"\"\"Configuration, read from the environment (never hard-code secrets).\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport os\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]\nTEMPLATES = ROOT / \"templates\"\nSITE = ROOT / \"site\"\n\nSECRET_KEY = os.environ.get(\"CMS_SECRET_KEY\", \"dev-only-not-for-production\")\nDATABASE_PATH = Path(os.environ.get(\"CMS_DATABASE\", ROOT / \"cms.db\"))\nSITE_TITLE = os.environ.get(\"CMS_SITE_TITLE\", \"Kenyon Men's Golf CMS\")\n# Set this to your Pages URL once you deploy, e.g.\n# https://yourname.github.io/iphs400-mp2-cms/\nBASE_PATH = os.environ.get(\"CMS_BASE_PATH\", \"\")\ntemplates:\nadmin\nbase.html\npublic\n\ntemplates/admin:\naccounts.html\nhello.html\nlogin.html\npost_form.html\nposts.html\n\ntemplates/public:\nhome.html\npost.html","is_error":false}]},"uuid":"ac0e0f2a-7bf5-4719-bb1d-8aa98311d473","timestamp":"2026-10-15T16:36:52.327Z","toolUseResult":{"stdout":"\"\"\"Content OR slug LIKE ?\",\n        (base, f\"{base}-%\"))}\n    slug, n = base, 2\n    while slug in taken:\n        slug, n = f\"{base}-{n}\", n + 1\n    return slug\n\n\ndef create_item(db_path: Path, kind: Kind, title: str, body: str,\n                author: Account, status: Status = Status.DRAFT) -> Item:\n    now = _now()\n    with db.connect(db_path) as conn:\n        cursor = conn.execute(\n            \"INSERT INTO items (kind, title, slug, body, status, author_id,\"\n            \" created_at, updated_at) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)\",\n            (kind, title, _unique_slug(conn, title, kind), body, status,\n             author.id, now, now),\n        )\n    return get_item(db_path, cursor.lastrowid)\n\n\ndef get_item(db_path: Path, item_id: int) -> Item | None:\n    with db.connect(db_path) as conn:\n        row = conn.execute(_SELECT + \"WHERE items.id = ?\", (item_id,)).fetchone()\n    return _from_row(row) if row else None\n\n\ndef list_items(db_path: Path, kind: Kind,\n               status: Status | None = None) -> list[Item]:\n    \"\"\"Newest first; only items with `status` when one is given.\"\"\"\n    with db.connect(db_path) as conn:\n        rows = conn.execute(\n            _SELECT + \"WHERE kind = ? AND status = COALESCE(?, status)\"\n            \" ORDER BY created_at DESC, items.id DESC\", (kind, status)).fetchall()\n    return [_from_row(row) for row in rows]\n\n\ndef update_item(db_path: Path, item_id: int, title: str, body: str,\n                slug: str | None = None, status: Status | None = None) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Change title and body; change the slug and status too when given.\n\n    Raises SlugTaken if the new slug belongs to another item.\n    \"\"\"\n    try:\n        with db.connect(db_path) as conn:\n            conn.execute(\n                \"UPDATE items SET title = ?, body = ?, slug = COALESCE(?, slug),\"\n                \" status = COALESCE(?, status), updated_at = ? WHERE id = ?\",\n                (title, body, slug, status, _now(), item_id),\n            )\n    except sqlite3.IntegrityError as exc:\n        raise SlugTaken(slug) from exc\n\n\ndef set_status(db_path: Path, item_id: int, status: Status) -> None:\n    with db.connect(db_path) as conn:\n        conn.execute(\"UPDATE items SET status = ?, updated_at = ? WHERE id = ?\",\n                     (status, _now(), item_id))\n\n\ndef delete_item(db_path: Path, item_id: int) -> None:\n    with db.connect(db_path) as conn:\n        conn.execute(\"DELETE FROM items WHERE id = ?\", (item_id,))\n\"\"\"The FastAPI application.\n\nThe admin console lives under /admin and needs a login (/login); a preview\nof the public site answers at /. Routes live in their own modules under\napp/routes/ and are included here. Keep this file small.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom fastapi import FastAPI, Request\nfrom fastapi.responses import RedirectResponse\nfrom starlette.middleware.sessions import SessionMiddleware\n\nfrom app import db, settings\nfrom app.routes import accounts, auth, console, posts, public\nfrom app.web import LoginRequired\n\n\ndef create_app(db_path: Path | None = None,\n               site_dir: Path | None = None) -> FastAPI:\n    app = FastAPI(title=\"IPHS 400 MP2 CMS\")\n    app.state.db_path = db_path or settings.DATABASE_PATH\n    # Where site updates write; tests pass a temporary directory.\n    app.state.site_dir = site_dir or settings.SITE\n    db.init(app.state.db_path)\n\n    # Signed session cookie that ends when the browser closes (shared laptop).\n    app.add_middleware(SessionMiddleware, secret_key=settings.SECRET_KEY,\n                       session_cookie=\"cms_session\", max_age=None,\n                       same_site=\"lax\")\n\n    @app.exception_handler(LoginRequired)\n    def to_login(request: Request, exc: LoginRequired):\n        return RedirectResponse(\"/login\", status_code=303)\n\n    app.include_router(auth.router)\n    app.include_router(console.router)\n    app.include_router(accounts.router)\n    app.include_router(posts.router)\n    app.include_router(public.router)\n    return app\n\n\napp = create_app()\n\"\"\"Demo data: one admin and one editor, so the console is usable straight away.\n\nscripts/seed_demo.py calls this with passwords from the environment; the tests\ncall it with fixed ones. Running it again leaves existing accounts alone.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom app import accounts, db\nfrom app.accounts import Role\n\nDEMO_EMAILS = {\n    Role.ADMIN: \"admin@example.test\",\n    Role.EDITOR: \"editor@example.test\",\n}\n\n\ndef seed_demo(db_path: Path, admin_password: str, editor_password: str) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"Create the demo accounts that do not exist yet; return the emails created.\"\"\"\n    db.init(db_path)\n    created = []\n    for role, password in ((Role.ADMIN, admin_password), (Role.EDITOR, editor_password)):\n        email = DEMO_EMAILS[role]\n        if accounts.find_by_email(db_path, email) is None:\n            accounts.create_account(db_path, email, password, role)\n            created.append(email)\n    return created\n#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"Create demo data so a grader (and you) can use the CMS immediately.\n\n    set -a; . ./.env; set +a\n    uv run python scripts/seed_demo.py\n\nCreates one admin and one editor account (app/seed.py), with passwords read\nfrom CMS_ADMIN_PASSWORD and CMS_EDITOR_PASSWORD, never hard-coded. Later\ntickets add demo posts and pages here.\n\nThe rubric expects this to run clean on a fresh clone with .env.example values\n(item E4), because the database itself is never committed.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport os\nimport sys\n\nfrom app import settings\nfrom app.seed import DEMO_EMAILS, seed_demo\n\n\ndef main() -> int:\n    admin_pw = os.environ.get(\"CMS_ADMIN_PASSWORD\")\n    editor_pw = os.environ.get(\"CMS_EDITOR_PASSWORD\")\n    if not admin_pw or not editor_pw:\n        print(\"Set CMS_ADMIN_PASSWORD and CMS_EDITOR_PASSWORD in .env \"\n              \"(copy .env.example).\")\n        return 1\n\n    created = seed_demo(settings.DATABASE_PATH, admin_pw, editor_pw)\n    for role, email in DEMO_EMAILS.items():\n        state = \"created\" if email in created else \"already exists\"\n        print(f\"{role:6}  {email}  ({state})\")\n    print(f\"Database: {settings.DATABASE_PATH}\")\n    return 0\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    sys.exit(main())\n\"\"\"Configuration, read from the environment (never hard-code secrets).\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport os\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]\nTEMPLATES = ROOT / \"templates\"\nSITE = ROOT / \"site\"\n\nSECRET_KEY = os.environ.get(\"CMS_SECRET_KEY\", \"dev-only-not-for-production\")\nDATABASE_PATH = Path(os.environ.get(\"CMS_DATABASE\", ROOT / \"cms.db\"))\nSITE_TITLE = os.environ.get(\"CMS_SITE_TITLE\", \"Kenyon Men's Golf CMS\")\n# Set this to your Pages URL once you deploy, e.g.\n# https://yourname.github.io/iphs400-mp2-cms/\nBASE_PATH = os.environ.get(\"CMS_BASE_PATH\", \"\")\ntemplates:\nadmin\nbase.html\npublic\n\ntemplates/admin:\naccounts.html\nhello.html\nlogin.html\npost_form.html\nposts.html\n\ntemplates/public:\nhome.html\npost.html","stderr":"","interrupted":false,"isImage":false,"noOutputExpected":false},"serverClassifierContext":{"request":"927c09a9-e098-407a-948e-e8f1b1fff1a0","context":{"git_state":{"cwd":"/home/refiv/ubuncode/iphs400-mp2-cms","root":"/home/refiv/ubuncode/iphs400-mp2-cms","branch":"main","default_branch":null,"status":{"clean":false,"counts":{"staged":0,"modified":1,"untracked":null,"untracked_normal":1},"porcelain":null,"truncated":false},"visibility":{"origin":{"host":"github.com","remote":"RafaelFrias1/iphs400-mp2-cms","visibility":"public"},"push_remote":"origin","remotes":[{"name":"origin","host":"github.com","remote":"RafaelFrias1/iphs400-mp2-cms","visibility":"public"}],"visibility_cache":[{"host":"github.com","remote":"RafaelFrias1/iphs400-mp2-cms","visibility":"public"}]}},"live_cwd":"/home/refiv/ubuncode/iphs400-mp2-cms","platform":"wsl"}},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"8a97e464-5557-41d7-b754-af28af25f592","permissionDecision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reasonType":"classifier"},"session_id":"3fe5d8d2-454b-407f-92b3-5945b5c07e19","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/home/refiv/ubuncode/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"ed3288d3-7efb-4637-b6c1-b203fb621bd9","version":"2.1.300","gitBranch":"main"}

Passwords\n# come from the environment there; in tests they are fixed and meaningless.\nDEMO_ACCOUNTS = {\n    \"admin\": {\"email\": DEMO_EMAILS[\"admin\"], \"password\": \"test-admin-pw\"},\n    \"editor\": {\"email\": DEMO_EMAILS[\"editor\"], \"password\": \"test-editor-pw\"},\n}\n\nCSRF_FIELD = re.compile(r'name=\"csrf_token\" value=\"([^\"]+)\"')\nACCOUNT_ROW = r'data-account-id=\"(\\d+)\" DEMO_ACCOUNTS[\"admin\"][\"password\"],\n              DEMO_ACCOUNTS[\"editor\"][\"password\"])\n    return path\n\n\n@pytest.fixture\ndef site_dir(tmp_path):\n    \"\"\"Where the console's site It rejects the\n    request with 403 unless the form's csrf_token matches the session's.\n  - `current_account` goes on every console route (the console router in\n    app/routes/console.py applies it to all of them). Someone who isn't\n    logged in, or whose account was deactivated, is sent to /login.\n  - `require_admin` goes on admin-only routes. It does what `current_account`\n    does, then refuses editors with 403, so a typed URL is denied, not just\n    a hidden link.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport hmac\nimport secrets\n\nfrom fastapi import Depends, Form, HTTPException, Request\nfrom fastapi.templating import Jinja2Templates\n\nfrom app import accounts, settings\nfrom app.accounts import Account\n\ntemplates = Jinja2Templates(directory=str(settings.TEMPLATES))\n\n\nclass LoginRequired(Exception):\n    \"\"\"Raised by `current_account`; create_app() turns it into a redirect.\"\"\"\n\n\ndef csrf_token(request: Request) -> str:\n    \"\"\"The session's CSRF token, created on first use. Put it in every form.\"\"\"\n    if \"csrf\" not in request.session:\n        request.session[\"csrf\"] = secrets.token_urlsafe(32)\n    return request.session[\"csrf\"]\n\n\ndef root(request: Request) -> str:\n    \"\"\"The relative path from this page back to the site root (\"\", \"../\", ...).\n\n    Console links are written as {{ root(request) }}admin/accounts, so they stay\n    relative yet still work when a form re-renders a page at a deeper URL such\n    as /admin/accounts/5/role.\n    \"\"\"\n    return \"../\" * (request.url.path.count(\"/\") - 1)\n\n\ndef when(timestamp: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"An ISO UTC timestamp as the console shows it: '2026-10-14 18:05 UTC'.\"\"\"\n    return f\"{timestamp[:16].replace('T', ' ')} UTC\"\n\n\ntemplates.env.globals[\"csrf_token\"] = csrf_token\ntemplates.env.globals[\"root\"] = root\ntemplates.env.filters[\"when\"] = when\n\n\ndef verify_csrf(request: Request, csrf_token: str = Form(\"\")) -> None:\n    expected = request.session.get(\"csrf\", \"\")\n    if not (expected and hmac.compare_digest(expected, csrf_token)):\n        raise HTTPException(status_code=403, detail=\"Invalid or missing CSRF token.\")\n\n\ndef current_account(request: Request) -> Account:\n    account_id = request.session.get(\"account_id\")\n    account = (accounts.get_account(request.app.state.db_path, account_id)\n               if account_id is not None else None)\n    if account is None or not account.active:\n        request.session.clear()\n        raise LoginRequired\n    return account\n\n\ndef require_admin(account: Account = Depends(current_account)) -> Account:\n    if not account.is_admin:\n        raise HTTPException(status_code=403, detail=\"Only admins can do that.\")\n    return account\n    assert not site_dir.exists()\n\n\n# --- which changes run a site update -----------------------------------------\n\ndef test_saving_a_draft_runs_no_site_update(client_as, post_form, site_dir):\n    c = client_as(\"editor\")\n    post_id = new_post(post_form, c, \"Practice schedule\")\n    post_form(c, f\"/admin/posts/{post_id}\", title=\"Practice schedule v2\",\n              body=\"\", action=\"save\")\n    assert not site_dir.exists()\n\n\ndef test_deleting_a_draft_runs_no_site_update(client_as, post_form, site_dir):\n    c = client_as(\"editor\")\n    publish_new(post_form, c, \"Already published\")\n    shutil.rmtree(site_dir)\n    draft_id = new_post(post_form, c, \"Never published\")\n    post_form(c, f\"/admin/posts/{draft_id}/delete\")\n    assert not site_dir.exists()\n\n\ndef test_editing_a_published_post_updates_the_site(client_as, post_form, site_dir):\n    c = client_as(\"editor\")\n    post_id = publish_new(post_form, c, \"Published by mistake\", \"oops\")\n    slug = slug_of(c, post_id)\n    response = post_form(c, f\"/admin/posts/{post_id}/unpublish\")\n    assert response.status_code == 303\n    assert \"Draft\" in c.get(f\"/admin/posts/{post_id}\").text\n    assert not post_file(site_dir, slug).exists()\n    assert \"Published by mistake\" not in CSRF, and who is logged in.\n\nThree dependencies do the guarding:\n\n  - `verify_csrf` goes on every state-changing (POST) route. It rejects the\n    request with 403 unless the form's csrf_token matches the session's.\n  - `current_account` goes on every console route (the console router in\n    app/routes/console.py applies it to all of them). Someone who isn't\n    logged in, or whose account was deactivated, is sent to /login.\n  - `require_admin` goes on admin-only routes. It does what `current_account`\n    does, then refuses editors with 403, so a typed URL is denied, not just\n    a hidden link.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport hmac\nimport secrets\n\nfrom fastapi import Depends, Form, HTTPException, Request\nfrom fastapi.templating import Jinja2Templates\n\nfrom app import accounts, settings\nfrom app.accounts import Account\n\ntemplates = Jinja2Templates(directory=str(settings.TEMPLATES))\n\n\nclass LoginRequired(Exception):\n    \"\"\"Raised by `current_account`; create_app() turns it into a redirect.\"\"\"\n\n\ndef csrf_token(request: Request) -> str:\n    \"\"\"The session's CSRF token, created on first use. Put it in every form.\"\"\"\n    if \"csrf\" not in request.session:\n        request.session[\"csrf\"] = secrets.token_urlsafe(32)\n    return request.session[\"csrf\"]\n\n\ndef root(request: Request) -> str:\n    \"\"\"The relative path from this page back to the site root (\"\", \"../\", ...).\n\n    Console links are written as {{ root(request) }}admin/accounts, so they stay\n    relative yet still work when a form re-renders a page at a deeper URL such\n    as /admin/accounts/5/role.\n    \"\"\"\n    return \"../\" * (request.url.path.count(\"/\") - 1)\n\n\ndef when(timestamp: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"An ISO UTC timestamp as the console shows it: '2026-10-14 18:05 UTC'.\"\"\"\n    return f\"{timestamp[:16].replace('T', ' ')} UTC\"\n\n\ntemplates.env.globals[\"csrf_token\"] = csrf_token\ntemplates.env.globals[\"root\"] = root\ntemplates.env.filters[\"when\"] = when\n\n\ndef verify_csrf(request: Request, csrf_token: str = Form(\"\")) -> None:\n    expected = request.session.get(\"csrf\", \"\")\n    if not (expected and hmac.compare_digest(expected, csrf_token)):\n        raise HTTPException(status_code=403, detail=\"Invalid or missing CSRF token.\")\n\n\ndef current_account(request: Request) -> Account:\n    account_id = request.session.get(\"account_id\")\n    account = (accounts.get_account(request.app.state.db_path, account_id)\n               if account_id is not None else None)\n    if account is None or not account.active:\n        request.session.clear()\n        raise LoginRequired\n    return account\n\n\ndef require_admin(account: Account = Depends(current_account)) -> Account:\n    if not account.is_admin:\n        raise HTTPException(status_code=403, {"parentUuid":"930efce1-9636-4daf-a685-dfc3594ba21c","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011Cg4MEaJH9R7ANNEhNJnwQ","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01AktwVPipkFKLYGjeAyuNgH","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/home/refiv/ubuncode/iphs400-mp2-cms/tests/test_t05_pages.py","content":"\"\"\"T05: the Coach manages pages; pages build the navigation (issue #6).\n\nSame two seams as T04. Over HTTP, an admin creates, edits, publishes,\nunpublishes and deletes pages at /admin/pages and editors are refused every\none of those actions. Rendering tests call render_site() into a temporary\ndirectory and read the navigation and home page it wrote.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport re\n\nimport pytest\nfrom fastapi.testclient import TestClient\nfrom test_t03_posts import new_post\nfrom test_t04_publish import publish_new, site_text\n\nfrom app.publish import render_site\n\n\ndef new_page(post_form, c: TestClient, title: str, body: str = \"\",\n             action: str = \"save\") -> int:\n    \"\"\"Create a page through the console; return the id it redirects to.\"\"\"\n    response = post_form(c, \"/admin/pages\", title=title, body=body, action=action)\n    assert response.status_code == 303, response.text\n    match = re.fullmatch(r\"/admin/pages/(\\d+)\", response.headers[\"location\"])\n    assert match, response.headers[\"location\"]\n    return int(match.group(1))\n\n\ndef page_slug(c: TestClient, page_id: int) -> str:\n    match = re.search(rf'data-page-id=\"{page_id}\" data-slug=\"([^\"]*)\"',\n                      c.get(\"/admin/pages\").text)\n    assert match, f\"No row for page {page_id}\"\n    return match.group(1)\n\n\ndef page_file(out, slug: str):\n    return out / \"pages\" / f\"{slug}.html\"\n\n\ndef nav_of(html: str) -> str:\n    match = re.search(r\"<nav[^>]*>(.*?)</nav>\", html, re.S)\n    assert match, \"No <nav> on the page\"\n    return match.group(1)\n\n\n# --- the admin manages pages -------------------------------------------------\n\ndef test_admin_creates_a_draft_page_with_the_post_fields(client_as, post_form,\n                                                          site_dir):\n    admin = client_as(\"admin\")\n    page_id = new_page(post_form, admin, \"Season Schedule\", \"- Oct 20, Denison\")\n    form = Over HTTP, an admin creates, edits, publishes,\nunpublishes and deletes pages at /admin/pages and editors are refused every\none of those actions. Rendering tests call render_site() into a temporary\ndirectory and read the navigation and home page it wrote.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport re\n\nimport pytest\nfrom fastapi.testclient import TestClient\nfrom test_t03_posts import new_post\nfrom test_t04_publish import publish_new, site_text\n\nfrom app.publish import render_site\n\n\ndef new_page(post_form, c: TestClient, title: str, body: str = \"\",\n             action: str = \"save\") -> int:\n    \"\"\"Create a page through the console; return the id it redirects to.\"\"\"\n    response = post_form(c, \"/admin/pages\", title=title, body=body, action=action)\n    assert response.status_code == 303, response.text\n    match = re.fullmatch(r\"/admin/pages/(\\d+)\", response.headers[\"location\"])\n    assert match, response.headers[\"location\"]\n    return int(match.group(1))\n\n\ndef page_slug(c: TestClient, page_id: int) -> str:\n    match = re.search(rf'data-page-id=\"{page_id}\" data-slug=\"([^\"]*)\"',\n                      c.get(\"/admin/pages\").text)\n    assert match, f\"No row for page {page_id}\"\n    return match.group(1)\n\n\ndef page_file(out, slug: str):\n    return out / \"pages\" / f\"{slug}.html\"\n\n\ndef nav_of(html: str) -> str:\n    match = re.search(r\"<nav[^>]*>(.*?)</nav>\", html, re.S)\n    assert match, \"No <nav> on the page\"\n    return match.group(1)\n\n\n# --- the admin manages pages -------------------------------------------------\n\ndef test_admin_creates_a_draft_page_with_the_post_fields(client_as, post_form,\n                                                          site_dir):\n    admin = client_as(\"admin\")\n    page_id = new_page(post_form, admin, \"Season Schedule\", \"- Oct 20, Denison\")\n    form = admin.get(f\"/admin/pages/{page_id}\").text\n    assert \"Season Schedule\" in form and \"Draft\" in form\n    assert 'class=\"created\"' in form and 'class=\"updated\"' in form\n    assert 'name=\"slug\"' in form\n    assert page_slug(admin, page_id) == \"season-schedule\"\n    assert not site_dir.exists()\n\n\ndef test_admin_publishes_a_page_and_it_reaches_the_site(client_as, post_form,\n                                                         site_dir):\n    admin = client_as(\"admin\")\n    page_id = new_page(post_form, admin, \"Season Schedule\",\n                       \"[Live scoring](https://golfstat.com)\", action=\"publish\")\n    page = page_file(site_dir, \"season-schedule\").read_text()\n    assert '<a href=\"https://golfstat.com\">Live scoring</a>' in page\n    assert \"Published\" in admin.get(f\"/admin/pages/{page_id}\").text\n\n\ndef test_editing_a_published_page_updates_the_site(client_as, post_form, site_dir):\n    admin = client_as(\"admin\")\n    page_id = new_page(post_form, admin, \"Travel Lineup\", \"Sam, Alex\",\n                       action=\"publish\")\n    post_form(admin, f\"/admin/pages/{page_id}\", title=\"Travel Lineup\",\n              slug=\"travel-lineup\", body=\"Sam, Jordan\", action=\"save\")\n    text = page_file(site_dir, \"travel-lineup\").read_text()\n    assert \"Sam, Jordan\" in text and \"Alex\" not in text\n\n\ndef test_unpublishing_a_page_removes_it_and_its_nav_link(client_as, post_form,\n                                                          site_dir):\n    admin = client_as(\"admin\")\n    publish_new(post_form, admin, \"A post\")\n    page_id = new_page(post_form, admin, \"Recruiting\", action=\"publish\")\n    assert post_form(admin, f\"/admin/pages/{page_id}/unpublish\").status_code == 303\n    assert \"Draft\" in admin.get(f\"/admin/pages/{page_id}\").text\n    assert not page_file(site_dir, \"recruiting\").exists()\n    assert \"Recruiting\" not in site_text(site_dir)\n\n\ndef test_deleting_a_published_page_removes_it(client_as, post_form, site_dir):\n    admin = client_as(\"admin\")\n    page_id = new_page(post_form, admin, \"Recruiting\", action=\"publish\")\n    response = post_form(admin, f\"/admin/pages/{page_id}/delete\")\n    assert response.status_code == 303\n    assert response.headers[\"location\"] == \"/admin/pages\"\n    assert not page_file(site_dir, \"recruiting\").exists()\n    assert admin.get(f\"/admin/pages/{page_id}\").status_code == 404\n\n\ndef test_saving_a_draft_page_runs_no_site_update(client_as, post_form, site_dir):\n    admin = client_as(\"admin\")\n    page_id = new_page(post_form, admin, \"Recruiting\")\n    post_form(admin, f\"/admin/pages/{page_id}\", title=\"Recruiting v2\",\n              slug=\"recruiting\", body=\"\", action=\"save\")\n    post_form(admin, f\"/admin/pages/{page_id}/delete\")\n    assert not site_dir.exists()\n\n\ndef test_pages_and_posts_share_one_slug_space(client_as, post_form):\n    admin = client_as(\"admin\")\n    publish_new(post_form, admin, \"Recruiting\")\n    assert page_slug(admin, new_page(post_form, admin, \"Recruiting\")) == \"recruiting-2\"\n\n\ndef test_a_post_id_is_not_a_page_and_a_page_id_is_not_a_post(client_as, post_form):\n    admin = client_as(\"admin\")\n    post_id = new_post(post_form, admin, \"A post\")\n    page_id = new_page(post_form, admin, \"A page\")\n    assert admin.get(f\"/admin/pages/{post_id}\").status_code == 404\n    assert admin.get(f\"/admin/posts/{page_id}\").status_code == 404\n\n\ndef test_console_links_admins_to_pages_but_not_editors(client_as):\n    assert \"admin/pages\" in client_as(\"admin\").get(\"/admin\").text\n    assert \"admin/pages\" not in
